# Steve Jobs Interview about the iPhone 3G - 6/9/2008

**Source**: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qSUTHa7ssoc

**Transcribed**: 2025-12-25 22:54

---

**[Speaker 1]**: All right.
**[Speaker 1]**: Well, we're curious about the business applications.
The iPhone for a lot of people is all about fun.
Why go after the business world?

**[Steve Jobs]**: Um, well, you know, the business world has bought a lot of iPhones in the last year.
Uh, there's a ton of CEOs and senior executives in in most of the Fortune 500 companies that have iPhones.
And there's a lot of employees that have them uh at home and they really want to use them at work.
So, uh we've been getting a lot of requests to to really uh figure out how to work uh with enterprise, push email, push calendars, push contacts, Microsoft Exchange basically.
And the security associated with an enterprise uh that we didn't have in the first iPhone.
And we've built all that stuff into the new iPhone.
Right out of the box.

**[Speaker 1]**: How important is that going after the BlackBerry, which has almost 50% market share?
I mean that's that's a lot of business if you get into that corporate market.

**[Steve Jobs]**: Uh, well, people are telling us they'd like to buy the iPhone if we had these features.
So we're we've added them and and uh uh we'll see what happens.
There seems to be a lot of demand.

**[Speaker 1]**: This is an odd concern, but do you worry at all that some CEOs may say, you know what?
This is great.
You've got all you've addressed all our security concerns for the email, but we don't want our employees to have a device that will draw their attention to music and television and videos and all these other things.

**[Steve Jobs]**: Uh, you know, I think we're starting to see a lot of business applications that use video and things like that as well, so.

**[Speaker 1]**: So you think it'll help in that front?

**[Steve Jobs]**: Yeah, I do.
I think people love the iPhone and they want to use it in business.

**[Speaker 1]**: Does it buy, you know, I'm carrying my BlackBerry and so many of us have these and you see people carrying them around everywhere you go.
Do you think that the iPhone can replace the BlackBerry, a BlackBerry like this in many work environments?
Is that something you strive for?

**[Steve Jobs]**: Well, that's up to customers to decide.
We're just going to give them the best iPhone we know how and they'll pick what they want.

**[Speaker 1]**: And tell me briefly about the new features of this iPhone that make it worthwhile over the last iPhone.
Speed being key to that?

**[Steve Jobs]**: Well, uh it's 3G speed, so it really downloads data dramatically faster and that's important when you're browsing as you know the iPhone has revolutionized mobile browsing in a way that no phone before it uh uh has.
And uh you know, faster browsing is really nice.
It's also great to download attachments in email.
And as you know, we display all Microsoft Word documents, all iWork documents and it's nice to be able to download whatever kind of attachments they are, be they PDFs or otherwise as fast as possible.
So getting fast data with 3G networking is great.
We've built in GPS uh for, you know, location based services, which is exploding on the iPhone.
And we've built in the full enterprise support, we've built in the support for third-party apps.
Uh, we're going to be selling it in over 70 countries around the world by the end of this year.
And we've been able to get the price down to $199, which we hope will mean that most everyone who wants one can afford one.

**[Speaker 1]**: Do you think you'll meet your goal of 10 million sold?
Some analysts have expressed concern that you won't, maybe you need to get into that corporate marketplace to do that.

**[Steve Jobs]**: Well, we've said several times we're confident we're going to meet the goal of selling 10 million iPhones in 2008.

**[Speaker 1]**: Where I work, they make us carry cell phones in addition to our Blackberries to have some backup.
Any concerns that it's too much for one device?
Be it the battery life, be it applications freezing, it's just it's a lot, isn't it?
To pack into one device?
Is it possible one can really do everything?

**[Steve Jobs]**: Well, actually the, you know, the the parent company you work for Disney has been one of the companies that's been beta testing the iPhone and you might have seen uh the CIO in the video, they seem pretty happy with it.
So, who knows?

**[Speaker 1]**: All right.
And and uh just wrapping up, looking forward to a completely different topic, coming up this summer, uh someone you know well, Bill Gates is retiring.
In in preparation for that, can I just ask you if you uh have any comments about looking back as he retires competition with him and his impact?

**[Steve Jobs]**: You know, today I'm just thinking about the iPhone 3G.

**[Speaker 1]**: All right.
Thought I'd try you while we're sitting here.
He's coming up.
All right.
Well, I appreciate it.

**[Steve Jobs]**: Thanks.

**[Speaker 1]**: Thanks very much.
Take care.

**[Steve Jobs]**: Sure.

**[Speaker 1]**: All righty.
